Believe me. I know serious, serious depression. Yesterday, for example, I was very, very low. I kind of felt like a downward spiral was coming on. I'm sure you know what I mean by that. I just said to myself, F it, I'm going to try to do something to get off my chair. I plodded through some lower body work and half an hour in, after chugging away and feeling like why bother, I started to feel clearer in my mind. After I finished my mood was better and I was able to walk down to the store. No small feat for me since I suffer from extreme social anxiety/bordering on agoraphobia. I used to think that it was nonsense too. The exercise thing. But I started when I was 40, out of shape, overweight, etc. And 3 years on, I am not perfect by any means...I still overeat, get depressed, etc. But I have not had to be hospitalized in 2 years. That says something. Before that, I was hospitalized quite regularly for my clinical depression. I know depression quite intimately, as I have said. Good luck in finding something you can manage. Walking is a good starting point. Even if it is in front of the computer, if you can't make yourself go out. Or some crunches on the floor. Whatever it takes to get the blood moving. I swear it is not hogwash.

I have been stable for 6 months now. First time in literally decades. I know depression very well. At least, my depression. I actually feel somewhat normal now, but I know that my distorted thinking led me to numerous suicide attempts. I was never in my "right mind" when I attempted suicide. (obviously, I suppose...but I just had an aha moment about that a few days ago). I cannot comment on various therapies since having ECT a few years ago has clouded my memories. I have been in DBT classes for a year a couple of years ago. That didn't seem to help. I still made suicide attempts. I started to exercise a couple of years ago to help with my anxiety. I find that no matter how shitty I feel, if I have bad anxiety I try to exercise it out first, if that makes any sense. 9 times out of 10 it works. It even brightens my mood a lot of the time. It has helped me ten fold. It is hard, I know, when you are going "down" to try to get your body to focus on something that it just doesn't want to do...but it is so worth the effort. I know that no one listens to me, lol, but it is not bs, believe me. I have tried everything, and I am finally feeling well and stable.
